messages.content: "Can you tell me the net worth of the famous footballer Lionel Messi in Euros? After that, I would like to know the net worth of the basketball player LeBron James in British Pounds. Also, I'm curious about the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person who weighs 85 kilograms and is 180 centimeters tall using the metric system. Lastly, could you calculate the BMI of another person who weighs 200 pounds and is 6 feet 2 inches tall using the imperial system?"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

message.reasoning:
We need to call two functions: celebrity_net_worth_get twice, and calculate_bmi twice. For Messi in Euros, we need to specify currency "EUR". For LeBron in GBP, currency "GBP". For BMI metric: weight 85 kg, height 180 cm, unit default metric. For BMI imperial: weight 200 pounds, height 6 feet 2 inches. But the calculate_bmi function expects weight in kilograms and height in centimeters. It also has optional unit param. But we can pass weight in pounds and height in inches? The function signature says weight: number, height: number, unit?: string. It says weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. But we can pass weight in pounds and height in inches if unit is 'imperial'? The description says "Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'." So we can pass weight in pounds and height in inches if unit is 'imperial'. So for second BMI: weight 200 pounds, height 6 feet 2 inches. We need to convert height to inches: 6 feet 2 inches = 6*12 + 2 = 74 inches. So weight 200, height 74, unit 'imperial'.

Thus we need to call calculate_bmi twice: first with weight 85, height 180, unit default metric. Second with weight 200, height 74, unit 'imperial'.

Also call celebrity_net_worth_get twice: first with name "Lionel Messi", currency "EUR". Second with name "LeBron James", currency "GBP".

We need to output the results. We'll call functions in order: Messi, LeBron, BMI metric, BMI imperial.
